cim_eredeti: More American Shoppers Say They’ll Use Gemini This Holiday Season Over Other AI
szoveg_eredeti:
A new survey suggests Americans who use AI for shopping prefer Gemini over ChatGPT. The finding underscores why brands need to be visible across different AI platforms this holiday season.

The survey was commissioned by email and SMS marketing platform Omnisend, which partnered with market research firm Cint to better understand consumer intent this holiday season across four markets. The survey polled 4,363 consumers last August in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia. Only about one-third of U.S. consumers are planning to use AI for their shopping needs. At 34 percent, it’s the lowest in the survey, compared to the U.K. (36 percent), Canada (39 percent), and Australia (40 percent).

Among these U.S.-based AI users, Gemini has overtaken ChatGPT, with 53 percent of respondents saying they plan to use Google’s AI platform compared with 46 percent for OpenAI’s chatbot. Other platforms did not come close. The next was Microsoft Copilot at 18 percent.

“AI is now a tool many people use regularly when they shop, and the assistant they choose is changing fast,” said Marty Bauer, director of sales and partnerships at Omnisend. “In the U.S., Gemini’s rise means retailers can’t optimize for ChatGPT alone; they need to be visible wherever AI search sends shoppers.”

Consumers in the U.K., Canada and Australia said they rely on ChatGPT for shopping research.

“At the same time, shoppers are worried about the credibility of the information that AI provides. Genuine reviews are paramount, as they build the trust that eventually leads to conversions,” he added.

Beyond how shoppers use AI, the survey also examined other parts of the gift-giving process such as their preferred online marketplace. In the U.S., Walmart topped Amazon, 67 percent compared to 62 percent. This was followed by the 21 percent who chose Temu and the 15 percent who picked Shein. The survey found that most shoppers plan to purchase gifts for family and friends, but one-third of Americans, especially those under 35, will also buy presents for themselves.

When it comes to the actual gifts, clothing is their first choice. However, the survey noted that this year clothing shares the spot with gift cards.

“When gift cards first appeared, they offered a way to give experiences instead of material items. In recent years, however, they acquired a reputation as a last-minute cop-out gift,” Bauer said. “Nowadays, they’re regaining popularity because they offer a convenient way to balance your gift budget,” he added. “You can set a clear spending limit.”
